newsitem.title: USA: Six rape probes reported at South Carolina base.
newsitem.headline: Six rape probes reported at South Carolina base.

text.p: The local rape crisis agency has been called to Fort Jackson six times since July, 1995, to investigate reports of soldiers raping other soldiers, an official with the centre said Friday.

Three of the cases reported at the U.S. Army training facility near Columbia involved drill sergeants and the others peers of the alleged victims, said Columbia Rape Crisis Network director Donna Smith, who was to meet with the post commander, Gen. William Bolt, to show him the agency's report.

Army spokesman Doug Cook acknowledged this week that two rape investigations were under way at the base, which trains more soldiers than any other Army installation. Base statistics show 30 allegations of sexual misconduct in the past year, with 27 proven to have merit, Cook said.

In the wake of a sex scandal at the Aberdeen Proving Ground in Maryland, all Army bases around the country are looking into reports of sexual misconduct. A toll-free number has been set up to receive reports.
